children: Nvidia (NVDA, Financials),-backed data center operator Firmus Grid has started premarketing a potential A$7 billion listing in Australia, giving investors another look at the infrastructure spending building around the AI boom.

Firmus began speaking with investors Thursday ahead of its planned listing on the Australian Securities Exchange, according to IFR. A term sheet sent to investors said the institutional bookbuild is expected to run from Oct. 6 to Oct. 7, with the prospectus due Oct. 8.
Retail investors are expected to be able to bid for shares from Oct. 12 through Oct. 19.

The company, founded in 2019 by Oliver Curtis, Tim Rosenfield and Jonathan Levee, could raise as much as $5.5 billion in the offering. An additional $500 million could be raised through a greenshoe option if demand allows.
Firmus operates data center infrastructure, putting the planned IPO squarely in the middle of the massive investment cycle surrounding artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.
For Nvidia, the connection is another example of how demand for AI computing is extending beyond chips into the power and infrastructure needed to run increasingly large data centers.
The next catalyst is the start of Firmus' institutional bookbuild on Oct. 6, when investor demand should give a clearer picture of how the market values the AI infrastructure operator.

title: Nvidia-Backed Firmus Grid Just Made a $7 Billion IPO Move
